findings.title: Note misstates the Case 4 walk-terminal candidate counts it labels [F]
findings.detail: Section 2 of the note says the terminal state has 76 single-step candidates: 36 are clean but do not raise L1, and 40 are rejected. results.json `walk_terminal_blockers` has n_candidates = 72, of which 36 are clean_not_up and 36 are rejected. The per-rule list adds up to 38 rule hits, or 41 with terminal_off_trace, because some candidates carry two rules. So '40' and '76' match neither count. The per-rule numbers themselves (min_trace_width 10, die_edge_margin 8, …) are correct, and the conclusion that every power feature sits at its rule minimum does not depend on this.
findings.evidence: results.json layouts.2D_Case_4.variants.R0.degrade.walk_terminal_blockers: n_candidates 72; outcomes clean_not_up 36, die_edge_margin 7, die_edge_margin+wire_length 1, die_spacing 2, edge_margin 5, min_spacing 7, min_trace_width 6, min_trace_width+terminal_off_trace 3, min_trace_width+wire_landing 1, wire_landing 3, wire_length 1 (36 rejected)
findings.suggested_check: Replace 76/40 with 72/36 and say that the per-rule hits overlap.

findings.title: Small factual or citation slips in the note
findings.detail: (a) The note says 2R has 22 R3 fields and Case 6 has 21; results.json has 23 and 20 R3 entries. (b) It says DesignRules.min_wire_length is marked 'placeholder' at rules.py line 31. Line 31 carries no such mark; the module docstring (line 6) calls all defaults placeholders. (c) The list of registered specs leaves out E901, an unrelated canary. None of these changes a conclusion.

findings.title: 'O003 does not require the lower bound' is stated as settled, but the objective text allows another reading
findings.detail: The note quotes the bondability clause (objective.yaml lines 61-63), which bounds the gate wire from above only. The clause that introduces scope_in, however, reads 'design rules at least as strict as the reference's own, measured on the snapped reconstruction and frozen in E008's spec'. If that list is read as illustrative rather than exhaustive, removing a measured minimum makes the rules less strict than the reference's own. Ranked change #1 (drop min_signal_wire_length) is labelled (i), a code change under a new freeze, not (ii), a criteria change, and that label depends on this reading. CLAUDE.md asks for ambiguity to be flagged. The 2R diagnosis itself (min_signal_wire_length is the one binding rule) holds either way.
findings.evidence: project/objectives/O003/objective.yaml lines 53-65; note section 1 'Conclusion: O003 does not require the lower bound'; section 5 item 1 labelled (i)
findings.suggested_check: Present the classification of change #1 as an interpretation for the founder, not as a fact.

findings.title: Two checklist facts are hard-coded or incomplete
findings.detail: checklist_facts sets `identical_dies` to True as a literal, not from the layout, yet results.json shows it beside the computed facts. `power_wires_per_die` counts only dies that have at least one wire starting on their source pad, so a die with no wires would be missing rather than reported as 0. The note's checklist answers to Q2 and Q4 cite other sources or agree with the data, so no conclusion is affected.
findings.suggested_check: Compute identical_dies from the die outlines and pads, and seed per_die with every die index.

findings.title: The Case 4 'no degradation-rule change reaches the target' result is a hill-climb limit, not a proof
findings.detail: P1 (1.260) and P2 (1.240) are greedy L1 climbs over a fixed candidate set. The note says so itself ('A hill-climb is not a proof that no D exists'). The negative result therefore applies only to the move sets tried.
